intro.h2: Old house nerds with a design-build plan
paragraphs: Kitchen remodeling in Portland gets tricky when the house is a hundred years old. Rooms are small, walls hide surprises, and the trim is worth saving. Craftsman Design and Renovation has spent over 25 years on exactly these homes, from Laurelhurst bungalows to a 1940 Tudor near Mt Tabor.

The team calls itself a group of old house nerds who geek out on original woodwork and the perfect rafter tail. On a 1902 kitchen in Northwest Portland, they replicated stained wood, v-groove wainscot and leaded glass transoms, then set a soapstone counter at the center. The goal on every job is the same: a room that works for today and looks like it was always there.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Portland, plus baths, basements and additions

items.name: Kitchen Remodels
items.blurb: After a design agreement, the designers draft concept drawings so you can see the layout and how your budget is spent before building starts. Most kitchens include custom cabinetry and shelving, new counters and flooring, a decorative backsplash, and new overhead and task lighting.

image.alt: 1913 Hawthorne kitchen remodel in Portland with blue painted cabinets, quartzite countertops, skylight and stainless range

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: New fixtures, glass shower enclosures, vanities and counters, custom cabinetry, flooring, lighting, and upgrades to ventilation and plumbing. The team drafts the plans, sources unusual materials when a period look calls for them, and handles the carpentry and finish work itself.

image.alt: 1910 Kings Hill bathroom in Portland with pedestal sink, recessed medicine cabinet, white subway tile and black-and-white mosaic border

items.name: Whole House Remodels
items.blurb: A study of your home and nearby houses from the same era guides the design, so every room reads as one whole. Work can happen all at once or in phases, with each phase planned so it sets up the next.

image.alt: 1916 Richmond Craftsman whole house remodel in Portland with sage green cabinets, wood-trimmed windows and a farmhouse sink

items.name: Basement Remodels
items.blurb: Turn a laundry and storage level into a family room, office, guest suite, wine cellar or extra bathroom. The design keeps the new space in step with the rest of your older home while adding the square footage you need.

image.alt: 1950 Laurelhurst Rambler basement remodel with stone fireplace wall, teal sofa, recessed lights and daylight windows

items.name: Additions and Exteriors
items.blurb: Bump-outs, sunrooms, porches, garages and full additions designed to look original to the house, with siding, trim and rooflines matched to the era. Award-winning examples include a 1935 Tudor Revival sunroom and a 1906 Craftsman addition.

image.alt: 1906 SE Portland cottage addition with green siding, covered front porch and restored foursquare roofline

about.h2: From an attic office to SE 27th Avenue
about.text: Wade Frietag started Craftsman Design and Renovation in the attic of his 1905 Craftsman home, out of a love for Portland's historic houses. The firm moved to SE Division Street in 2004, above Rejuvenation on SE Grand in 2012, and to SE Belmont in 2015. Today Bill Myles, a Certified Remodeler, owns the company. His team includes designers Erika Rice and Stephanie Capretto, both CKBD, project manager Ryan Murphy and lead carpenters Pete Kelly and Nathan Maszy, both CLC. Clients have called them forensic architects for the way they read an old house.

image.alt: Bill Myles, owner of Craftsman Design and Renovation in Portland, OR

process.h2: Four phases from first visit to final walk-through

steps.title: We partner
steps.text: An in-home or online consultation, then a flexible design retainer with a realistic target budget and an on-site survey with measuring and photos.

steps.title: We design
steps.text: Floor plans and 3D drawings, then early fixture and finish picks, a detailed scope of work and a preliminary estimate.

steps.title: We prepare
steps.text: A fixed-cost construction agreement, permit drawings with any needed engineering, and a prestart meeting with your project manager and lead carpenter.

steps.title: We build
steps.text: The work zone is sealed off to limit dust and noise, cleaned to broom clean daily, and reviewed with you at weekly meetings.

service_area.text: The office is at 837 SE 27th Ave, in the middle of the older neighborhoods the team loves most. Their project list runs through Mt Tabor, North Tabor, Laurelhurst, Hawthorne, Richmond, Sellwood, Eastmoreland, Irvington, Alameda, Grant Park, Rose City and Northwest Portland, with award-winning work in Lake Oswego and Raleigh Hills. If your house was built before most of your neighbors were born, call and ask.

faq.h2: Common questions about remodeling an older Portland home

items.q: What does a kitchen remodel with you usually cost?
items.a: The firm's FAQ page lists kitchen remodels in the $150,000 to $250,000 range. Your number depends on scope, structure and finishes. A flexible design retainer and a realistic target budget come first, then a preliminary estimate during design and a fixed-cost construction agreement before building starts.

items.q: Will my remodel match the rest of my 1910s house?
items.a: That is the core of the work. On a 1902 kitchen the team replicated stained wood, v-groove wainscot and leaded glass transoms. For whole houses, they compare your home with others built in the same era to guide the design, then blend in what you need today.

Yes. Craftsman Design and Renovation is registered with the Oregon Construction Contractors Board as CCB#131520. Owner Bill Myles holds the Certified Remodeler designation, two designers are Certified Kitchen and Bath Designers, and two lead carpenters are Certified Lead Carpenters. Ask to see the registration before you sign.

items.q: Can we live at home during construction?
items.a: Many clients do. The construction area is sealed off to cut noise and dust in the rest of the house, the site is left broom clean at the end of every workday, and staff follow a written Health and Safety Plan that you review before the contract.

Call (503) 239-6200 or request a consultation online. The first meeting can be in your home or online, and it is a chance for both sides to see if the project is a good fit before you sign a design agreement.
